items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: With Alphonse? With Trent, yeah, with the big orchestra.

ctx.x: Oh, Titty-Tat. I can think of his name. Where is he from? New Orleans. No, Titty-Tat, Titty-Tat's from New Orleans. Oh, Titty-Tat. I'm talking about Titty-Tat. The trumpet. The trumpet was living on Mount Main. Hot doggie. Used to keep the name. Yeah, he played it upside down. And then he used to play that Titty-Tit-Tat, you know, that box trumpet. In other words. 40 years ago. He was on a circus type. Yeah, it was a circus type. A circus type playing. Yes, sir. He came off a circus and came with us. That man…

Yeah. Red Island was playing a lot of flatted fifths back in 1929. I got records of that and all that stuff, you know. Higginbotham Blues, the ends of a flatted fifth in 1929. That's what J.C. Higginbotham was playing. He was out of that Louis Russell group, you know.
